title: fix(types): an unevaluable hook condition's refusal answers 400 VALIDATION_ERROR at every data door
body:
Fixes #24662
Clause-②: no

A write that an authored hook `condition` refused, because the condition compiled and then could not be evaluated on the record it was judging, now answers a coded refusal: `400` with code `VALIDATION_ERROR`, on the REST data doors and on the runtime dispatcher's `/data` door. Before, it answered `500 INTERNAL_ERROR`, and `@objectstack/rest` logged it as `[REST] Unhandled error`. Fail-closed does not move: the row is still not written.

## What was wrong (measured on `origin/main` `eadea5720`)

The card's repro was driven through a real engine (`ObjectQL` with a sqlite `SqlDriver`) and a real `ObjectStackProtocolImplementation`. The hook was bound by the engine's own `bindHooksToEngine`: `beforeInsert` on `inquiry`, with the condition `record.name.startsWith('qa-fc') && int(record.name) > 0`. The request was `POST /api/v1/data/inquiry` with `name: "qa-fc-abc"`.

| door | before | after |
|---|---|---|
| `RestServer` `POST /data/:object` (`mapDataError`) | `500 {"error":"Internal server error","code":"INTERNAL_ERROR"}` plus `[REST] Unhandled error: HookConditionError: ...` | `400 {"error":"Hook 'qa_failclosed' could not evaluate its condition (runtime: int() type error: cannot convert to int) — operation aborted.","code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","object":"inquiry"}`, no log line |
| `RestServer` `POST /data/:object/createMany` (`handleRouteError`) | the same `500` and the same log line | the same `400` body, no log line |
| dispatcher `/data` (the throw leaves `dispatch()`; `@objectstack/hono`'s catch-all renders it through `declaredEnvelopeForThrow`) | `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` declines it, so the fallback arm answers `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` with the hook's message | `400 {"success":false,"error":{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Hook 'qa_failclosed' could not evaluate ..."}}` |
| dispatcher `/data` (`dispatcher-plugin`'s `errorResponseBase` reads `resolveThrownHttpError`) | `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` | `400 VALIDATION_ERROR` |
| `POST /data/:object/batch` row (`toRowApiError`) | `{"code":"INTERNAL_ERROR","message":"The create of this record failed. The reason is in the server log."}` | `{"code":"VALIDATION_ERROR","message":"Hook 'qa_failclosed' could not evaluate ...","httpStatus":400}` |

In every row above the inquiry table held 0 rows after the request.

Why it happened: `HookConditionError` (`packages/objectql/src/hook-wrappers.ts`) carries no `status` and no `code`, on purpose. Its docblock rules that a fact on it reaches the wire through the ADR-0112 vocabulary as a decision. No boundary had decided, so the class matched nothing in `classifyDataError` and nothing in `resolveThrownHttpError`, and each door fell to its unclassified 500.

## The fix: one recogniser, read by both rules

- **`packages/types/src/hook-condition-refusal.ts` (new).** `unevaluableHookConditionRefusal(err)` recognises the class by its declared `name` and its declared `reason: 'unevaluable'`, never by message text. `@objectstack/types` cannot import `@objectstack/objectql`. It answers `{ status: 400, code: standardErrorCodeForHttpStatus(400) }`. It is not exported from the package index, so the public surface does not move.
- **`resolveThrownHttpError` (`thrown-http-error.ts`).** The shape is a declaration of both halves there, as the validation shape already is: `declaredStatus: 400`, `declaredCode: 'VALIDATION_ERROR'`. This one change serves the dispatcher's exits, both Hono doors (whose declared-envelope gate needs a declared status and a registered code) and the batch rows.
- **`structuredCodeAnswer` (`data-error-classification.ts`).** A new arm sits beside its precedent, the `VALIDATION_FAILED` arm. Both REST doors ask it first, so the single-record door and the bulk doors answer alike.

The landing points widen the claim's surface in one place. The claim named `data-error-classification.ts` and `error-response.ts`. Measured, the runtime twin does not read the classification at all; it reads `resolveThrownHttpError`. So `thrown-http-error.ts`, in the same package, carries the second reader, and the recogniser gets its own module. `packages/rest/src/error-response.ts` needs no change: the log verdict already reads the declaration off `resolveThrownHttpError` (`isDeclaredClientRefusal`). Nothing under `packages/objectql/**` or `packages/spec/**` is touched.

## The code choice, and why it is not a new code

- **Status `400`: the nearest landed precedent.** ADR-0058's 2026-08 addendum lists the hook `condition` (#4775) beside the object validation predicate (#4649) as one family: an unevaluable write gate fails closed. Measured on the same door, a validation rule whose condition is the card's expression answers `400` (code `VALIDATION_FAILED`, `fields[0].constraint.reason: 'unevaluable'`). Its sentence comes from the same `cel-fault.ts` as the hook's. The refusal turns on this record's values: another record can pass the same condition, and retrying the same request cannot.
- **Code `VALIDATION_ERROR`, not the sibling's `VALIDATION_FAILED`.** `VALIDATION_FAILED`'s contract is the per-field `fields[]` envelope that a form maps onto its inputs, and a hook's gate addresses no field. `VALIDATION_ERROR` is the `StandardErrorCode` member that ADR-0112's status map names for a `400` whose producer declared no more specific code. The batch rows and the nested-envelope doors already derive it for an un-coded `400` refusal. No code is minted and no ledger row is added, so `Clause-②: no` holds as the claim declared it.
- **The spec seat's branch test.** "Does this defect give a consumer a branch it could act on differently? No ⇒ widen the existing member's comment/message; yes ⇒ new code under the pre-approved class." The answer is no. A consumer branches on this exactly as it branches on a generic `400`: do not retry the same request, and show the message. The finer fact ("the author's expression faulted") already has a discriminator on the sibling, `constraint.reason: 'unevaluable'`. Measured on objectui `cd4623d`, no production file reads that discriminator, so no consumer branch exists that a new top-level code would serve. The existing member's meaning is unchanged, and the new module's docblock records why it covers this case.

## Scope: the `unevaluable` reason only

`reason: 'uncompilable'` (the condition never compiled) keeps its sanitised `500` and its `[REST] Unhandled error` line, and it is pinned as a control. It does not turn on the request: every write to the object fails until an author fixes the metadata. The gate already logs it at `error` when the hook is bound. Its message ends with `fix the expression:` followed by the condition SOURCE, which no sibling refusal puts on the wire. The platform checklist records that the metadata door refuses such a condition at authoring time (`422 INVALID_METADATA`), so it reaches this gate only from hooks bound outside that door.

## What the client message names

The arm relays the producer's message, as the `VALIDATION_FAILED` arm relays its own. It names the hook, the CEL fault in one line and, when known, the key the condition read (the shared `describeCelFault` detail). It never names the condition source or a record value; the e2e pin asserts that neither the source nor `qa-fc-abc` appears in the body. These are the facts the sibling validation-rule refusal already carries, by construction, because both come from one sentence builder.

## The log

The REST doors no longer print `[REST] Unhandled error` for this refusal, and they print no other line. Precedent: AGENTS.md, "Degradation log levels": "a failure handed to the CALLER is not a degradation at all … Do not bolt a `logger.error` onto such a site". It also follows `isDeclaredClientRefusal` (#23932), which reads a declaration off the thrown error rather than growing the `isExpectedRouteError` list by a name. `resolveThrownHttpError` now reports this shape's status and code, so the verdict needs no edit. The runtime exits log only 5xx (`logServerFault`), so a `400` costs no line there either. The operator signal that remains is the uncompilable reason's bind-time `error` line, which is unchanged. See the acceptance notes for the producer-side gap.

## Pins (each asserts status and code, not "it threw")

- `packages/rest/src/rest-hook-condition-unevaluable-refusal.test.ts`, real engine and real `RestServer` handlers:
  - the card's request answers `400` with the exact body, the source and value are absent, the row is absent, and there is no `[REST] Unhandled error` line;
  - `createMany` answers the same;
  - CONTROL: a hook that refuses on purpose (`403 PERMISSION_DENIED`) answers byte for byte as before;
  - CONTROL: the uncompilable reason keeps `500 INTERNAL_ERROR` and exactly one `[REST] Unhandled error` line. This is also the positive control for the log spy, under `OS_REST_LOG=info`.
- `packages/runtime/src/domains/data-hook-condition-refusal.test.ts`, the dispatcher `/data` door on the `data-write-request-gate.test.ts` rig:
  - the card's request: `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` (imported, not restated) answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, `resolveThrownHttpError` answers `400 VALIDATION_ERROR`, and the row is absent;
  - CONTROL: the deliberate refusal is returned as `403` with an unchanged body;
  - CONTROL: uncompilable is still declined by `declaredEnvelopeForThrow` and resolves to `500`.
- `packages/types/src/hook-condition-refusal.test.ts`: the recogniser, and agreement between the two rules that read it, on source.
- `packages/rest/src/error-response-structured-arm-door-parity.test.ts`: one more §1 case, so the single, bulk and route doors stay equal for this class. The arm is name-keyed, so the code-literal census there cannot see it.

## Pin sweep (repo-wide, one round)

I searched the repo for the wire answer of an unevaluable hook condition (`INTERNAL_ERROR` or `500` paired with a hook condition, `HookConditionError`, and `could not evaluate its condition`):

- `packages/qa/dogfood/test/hook-after-condition-rollback.dogfood.test.ts`: three assertions of `{ status: 500, code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR' }` for an `afterInsert` condition that reads `previous` on an insert now assert `{ status: 400, code: 'VALIDATION_ERROR' }`. The header sentence that called the refusal the sanitised 500 is corrected.
- `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/records-forms.json`, `records-forms.object-hook-lifecycle` acceptance[8] (revision 6 to 7): the verify text recorded the 500 against #24619 row (b). It now states the coded refusal and scores a 500 as a FAIL, and the server-log evidence is dropped.
- `content/docs/automation/hooks.mdx`: one sentence now gives the wire answer of a refused write.
- Other hits that stay as they are: `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.bulk-record-not-found.test.ts` throws a bare `Error` carrying the hook's text (not the class) and asserts that the text is absent; `showcase-anonymous-deny-surfaces.dogfood.test.ts` asserts that a message does not mention the class; the objectql unit suites pin the engine, not the wire.

## Ablation (one leg for the one changed behaviour)

The fix was committed first (`3ed86f196`). The mutation went through `node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in WRAP mode, so its trap restored the file. The anchor was `if (e?.name !== 'HookConditionError' || ...` and the replacement used the name `'HookConditionError_ABLATED'`, so the recogniser matches nothing.

- Landed: anchor count 1 to 0, blob `6099c6874149` to `be145e442da8`. `@objectstack/types` was rebuilt, and `node scripts/ablation-dist-preflight.mjs @objectstack/types 'HookConditionError_ABLATED'` exited 0 (marker in `dist/`). The rest suites read types' `dist/`; the runtime suite aliases it to source.
- Mutated leg:
  - types pin: 3 failed, 2 passed;
  - rest e2e: 2 failed (the card's request and `createMany`, "expected 500 to be 400"), 2 passed (both controls);
  - parity: 1 failed (the new case), 65 passed;
  - runtime twin: 1 failed (`declaredEnvelopeForThrow` answered `undefined`), 2 passed (both controls).
- Restored: blob `6099c6874149` equals HEAD, `git diff HEAD` is empty, and the marker count on disk is 0. After a rebuild, the dist preflight with `--absent` exited 0 on a clean tree. Restored leg: types 5/5, rest e2e 4/4, parity 66/66, runtime 3/3.

## Tests and gates (final head `910352e21`)

- `@objectstack/types`: `vitest run --project local` gave 28 files / 764 passed, and `typecheck` exited 0. These ran at `3ed86f196`; the one later commit touches only a rest test file.
- `@objectstack/rest`: `pnpm --filter @objectstack/rest test` (local project) gave 301 files, 6099 passed and 326 skipped, at `3ed86f196`. `typecheck`, including `check:test-typecheck`, exited 0. The repo project's `error-response-structured-arm-door-parity.test.ts` and `error-response-sandbox-arm-message.test.ts` gave 2 files / 156 passed. `rest-hook-condition-unevaluable-refusal.test.ts` re-ran at `910352e21`: 5/5.
- `@objectstack/runtime` (targeted; the full suite is CI's): six data-door and error-envelope files gave 108 passed, and the repo project's `error-envelope.conformance.test.ts` gave 53 passed. `typecheck`, including `check:test-typecheck`, exited 0.
- Readers of the shared rule:
  - `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`: 6 batch-row files, 94 passed;
  - `@objectstack/core`: 4 import-runner files, 111 passed;
  - `@objectstack/plugin-hono-server`: full suite, 34 files / 422 passed;
  - `@objectstack/hono`: full suite, 11 files / 215 passed.
- Dogfood, once, on the final head: `hook-after-condition-rollback.dogfood.test.ts` ran against a booted stack and gave 5/5 with the flipped pins. `@objectstack/dogfood` `typecheck` exited 0.
- Derived gate families: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands` derived 96 commands at `910352e21`, and all 96 exited 0 (exit codes captured before any pipe, after a full `turbo run build`). The `--ran` reconciliation reads "96 derived famil(ies) accounted for — 96 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED".
- `pnpm lint` (`eslint . --no-inline-config`, the whole repo) at `910352e21` exited 0.
- The after-insert case in the rest e2e file was added after the ablation and was not ablated on its own. It reads the same arm, and the dogfood pin above is its booted-stack twin.
- `origin/main` was not merged in: the 12 commits ahead of the merge base touch none of the files this change reads or edits. The one overlap by file, `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts`, changes the exposure-gate read and not the batch-row seam. The merge queue rebuilds on current `main`.

## Acceptance notes

- **A `before*` unevaluable condition leaves no operator line.** The validation-rule sibling gets a WARN from its producer (`rule-validator.ts`: "predicate failed to evaluate … — write rejected"). An `after*` hook's fault is covered by the engine's warn-level `Insert operation failed` line, seen in the dogfood run. A `beforeInsert` hook's fault raised no line in these runs: the hook wrapper logs nothing for the unevaluable reason, and the engine line did not appear. A producer-side line would belong in `packages/objectql` (`hook-wrappers.ts`), which this dispatch holds off. Observation only; not filed.
- **The runtime door still relays an uncompilable condition's 500 message verbatim.** On the dispatcher `/data` door, `@objectstack/hono`'s fallback arm answers the uncompilable reason's `500` with its message, which quotes the condition source. That is the standing #5667 posture ("whether an undeclared 5xx stays legible is a standing decision this arm does not reopen"), and this PR does not move it. The REST doors withhold the same message. Noted, not filed, because it is a ruled posture.
